public_source: Gulati-Nechita-Park, arXiv:2509.15201v4, Example 5.8 and Proposition 2.12, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.15201v4. The source states that a particular pair (A,B), A=I_4+lambda*J_off and B=H_tilde-lambda*J_off, gives positive indecomposable DUC/CDUC maps for 1/2<=lambda<1. H_tilde has diagonal 1 and H_tilde_01=H_tilde_10=-1. The source's positivity and indecomposability assertions are named imports, not independently reproved here.
duc_rank_two_test: For the source's DUC convention (its Eq. (5)), the Choi operator is W=sum_ij A_ij[|ij>]+sum_(i!=j) B_ij |ii><jj|. The Schmidt-rank-two vector |00>+|11> has expectation A_00+A_11+B_01+B_10=1+1+2*(-1-lambda)=-2lambda. Hence it is negative for every lambda>0; in particular the source's entire positive-indecomposable interval is NOT 2-positive.
cduc_rank_two_test: For the source's CDUC convention (its Eq. (6)), the Choi operator is W'=sum_ij A_ij[|ij>]+sum_(i!=j) B_ij |ij><ji|. The Schmidt-rank-two vector |01>+|10> has expectation A_01+A_10+B_01+B_10=2lambda+2*(-1-lambda)=-2. Thus this second orientation is also not 2-positive anywhere in the source's interval.
limits: These are exact symbolic two-vector obstructions only. They do not test or challenge the cited positive-indecomposable conclusion, classify other parameter choices or families, or provide a 4x4 PPT/SN3 state. No novelty or independent review claim.
